Subject: Invoice INV-20270630 held — large usage spike / suspected double-counting

Hi David,

Quick note from Storify Finance — we've placed invoice INV-20270630 (due 2027-07-05) on hold pending clarification. Our AP team shows a +38% delta versus the prior month and the line item is labelled "session_tokens_eu". We believe a subset of calls across 2027-06-28 23:45–2027-06-29 00:15 UTC were double-counted (sessions split at midnight across two ingestion windows).

Can you: 
- Share a session-by-session export (raw event timestamps + session_id) for the Europe region for 2027-06-28/29,
- Confirm whether any batch-window change or deploy happened in that window,
- Provide the invoice-level VAT treatment guidance (we need to know if a credit note will be net of VAT or requires a new VAT invoice).

AP has paused the wire pending a reconciliation; they also asked for a written credit note rather than an informal adjustment. I attached the invoice PDF for reference.

Thanks — appreciate a quick triage.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Finance, Storify
attachments: [storify_invoice_INV-20270630.pdf]

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 09:02 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for flagging and for attaching the invoice.

Liam — I pulled the session-level export and a short summary is below. Full CSV attached (redwood_usage_window_query_20270629.csv).

What I see: 
- Between 2027-06-28T23:40:00Z and 2027-06-29T00:12:00Z we have ~14k sessions where session_id appears with two distinct attribution_window_id values. This aligns with the rollout of a small ingestion-logger change that adjusted the "window_boundary" behavior in EU by moving from a 60s trailing buffer to a 0s strict cutoff. The change was deployed at 2027-06-29T00:00:03Z UTC.
- Because many clients were mid-session at the boundary, those requests were recorded once in the pre-cut window and again as new sessions post-cut (different session_id variants). That explains the +38% token delta on the invoice line.

Proposed remediation: 
1) We can provide Storify with a corrective usage export that deduplicates session pairs by client_session_fingerprint and takes the earlier timestamp as canonical — this yields a provisional credit of 58,420 tokens (attached calc in the CSV).
2) Issue a formal credit note for the token value: EUR 3,125.60 (VAT treatment TBD by Hannah).
3) If AP releases the wire for the remainder of the invoice (net of the proposed credit) we can expedite the DocuSign credit note and finalize VAT fields.

Attaching files: redwood_usage_window_query_20270629.csv (session export + dedupe calc), proposed_credit_note_draft.pdf (internal draft).

Let me know if you want a different dedupe rule (e.g., prefer later session) — we can re-run quickly.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Billing Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood_usage_window_query_20270629.csv, proposed_credit_note_draft.pdf]

Thanks Ben / David — this is helpful and fast, appreciate it.

Storify AP — we will accept Redwood's provisional credit calculation (EUR 3,125.60) pending a formal credit note. Please: 
- Prepare a formal credit note that includes VAT fields and indicates the original invoice reference INV-20270630,
- Confirm VAT treatment: for cross-border service to an EU company we need the net amount and a reference to reverse-charge if applicable; Hannah, please advise and confirm the exact wording we should expect.
- We will release the wire for the remainder of the invoice once the credit note (PDF) is signed/acknowledged. Our treasury needs the DocuSign record for audit.

Liam (for AP) has copied our accounting contact Anna for sign-off. Anna, please confirm once you see the credit note.

Next steps: David/Ben — can you send the formal credit note (DocuSign link OK) by EOB today? Also include the CSV export you attached for our records.

Best,
Liam
